contradictions.contradiction_text: The Agency Summary & Certification page is signed by 'Larry Stokes' as Department Director dated 10/29/2025, but all organizational charts and division descriptions throughout the document consistently list 'Scott Stokes' as Director of ITD. These appear to be two different names for the same position, suggesting either a data entry error in the certification signature or the existence of two different individuals — one of whom (Larry) does not appear in the org charts.
contradictions.reference: Certification page: 'Larry Stokes Signature of Department Director: 10/29/2025'; Org chart page 6: 'Scott Stokes Director'; Agency performance report p. 250: 'L. Scott Stokes, Director'

contradictions.contradiction_text: The Aeronautics FY2025 Total Appropriation summary shows $41,352,700 total, but FY2025 Actual Expenditures for Aeronautics (TRFG) total only $12,914,000 — a gap of approximately $28.4M. A large reappropriation of $25,233,600 is shown as a legislative reappropriation reduction (DU 1.71), suggesting significant unspent funds were carried forward rather than expended.
contradictions.reference: Agency Summary: 'Aeronautics TRFG FY 2025 Total Appropriation 41,352,700 / FY 2025 Total Expenditures 12,914,000'; Decision unit 1.71: '22102 Dedicated (25,233,600)'

contradictions.contradiction_text: The FY2027 Budget Request for the Aeronautics appropriation unit (TRFG) total is stated as $4,843,600, while the FY2026 Total Appropriation was $41,760,700 — a reduction of approximately $36.9M. The document notes this is primarily due to removal of one-time reappropriation authority for airport development grants and Leading Idaho funding, but the magnitude of the drop from appropriation to request warrants scrutiny.
contradictions.reference: Agency Summary: 'Aeronautics TRFG FY2026 Estimated Expenditures 41,760,700 / FY2027 Total Request 4,843,600'

contradictions.contradiction_text: The FY2026 Estimated Expenditures for the Contract Construction & Right-of-Way Acquisition division (TRFF) are $850,517,200, while the FY2027 Total Request is only $608,992,000 — a reduction of $241.5M. The document attributes this to removal of one-time reappropriation authority, but the FY2025 Total Appropriation was $1,256,104,000 while actual expenditures were $695,224,600, indicating persistent large gaps between appropriation and actual spending.
contradictions.reference: Agency Summary table: 'Contract Construction TRFF FY2025 Total Appropriation 1,256,104,000 / FY2025 Total Expenditures 695,224,600 / FY2026 Original Appropriation 608,992,000 / FY2026 Estimated Expenditures 850,517,200 / FY2027 Total Request 608,992,000'

contradictions.contradiction_text: The State Highway Account - Dedicated/State Fund (26002) shows a projected ending unobligated cash balance of negative $174,203,400 by end of FY2027, despite total investments of $183,935,300. This structural negative cash position is a growing trend: FY24 ending balance was -$34,513,900; FY25 was -$63,604,300; FY26 estimate is -$118,735,700. The fund is increasingly relying on direct investments to maintain solvency.
contradictions.reference: Fund 26002 Analysis of Fund Balances Row 35: FY24 (34,513,900), FY25 (63,604,300), FY26 estimate (118,735,700), FY27 estimate -174,203,400; Row 36 Investments: consistently $183,935,300

contradictions.contradiction_text: The State Highway Account - Federal Fund (26003) similarly shows a deeply negative and worsening unobligated cash balance: FY24 -$10,908,000; FY25 -$69,554,200; FY26 estimate -$102,327,900; FY27 estimate -$139,075,500. Unlike Fund 26002, there are no direct investments to offset this. The fund relies on reappropriation authority to cover the gap between expenditures and available cash.
contradictions.reference: Fund 26003 Analysis of Fund Balances Row 35: FY24 (10,908,000), FY25 (69,554,200), FY26 (102,327,900), FY27 -139,075,500; Row 36: all zeros

contradictions.contradiction_text: The Aeronautics Fund 22102 Analysis of Fund Balances shows a negative ending unobligated cash balance of -$1,799,300 projected for FY26 and -$1,517,600 for FY27, yet the fund has direct investments of $1,998,984 — meaning the fund depends entirely on those investments to remain solvent. The FY2025 actual ending unobligated balance was positive $5,901,400, showing a dramatic deterioration.
contradictions.reference: Fund 22102 Analysis Row 35: FY25 5,901,400; FY26 (1,799,300); FY27 -1,517,600; Row 36: $1,998,984 investments; Row 37 (Ending Unobligated + Investments): FY26 $199,684; FY27 $481,384

contradictions.contradiction_text: Employee Jacob Stokes (Agency 290) received a $1,500 recruitment bonus on 06/21/2025. The Director of ITD is listed as Scott Stokes (also signed as 'L. Scott Stokes' in performance report). The shared surname is notable though not necessarily improper; however, hiring/bonus documentation for an employee with the same surname as the Director warrants verification of any familial relationship and compliance with nepotism policies.
contradictions.reference: Bonus Report: '290 311526 JACOB STOKES 1 1,500.00 USD REC RECRUITMENT-MORE THAN 6 MO 06/21/2025'; Agency Performance Report p.250: 'L. Scott Stokes, Director'

contradictions.contradiction_text: Employee Phillip Borresen (Employee 310409) appears in the bonus report under BOTH Agency 230 and Agency 290. He received a REN6 (retention less than 6 months) bonus of $1,500 under Agency 230 on 08/17/2024, and a REC (recruitment more than 6 months) bonus of $1,500 under Agency 290 on 06/07/2025. The dual-agency appearance suggests a transfer between agencies, but receiving both retention and recruitment bonuses across two agencies warrants verification.
contradictions.reference: Bonus Report: '230 310409 Phillip Borresen 1 1,500.00 USD REN6 RETENTION-LESS THAN 6 MO 08/17/2024' and '290 310409 Phillip Borresen 1 1,500.00 USD REC RECRUITMENT-MORE THAN 6 MO 06/07/2025'

contradictions.contradiction_text: Employee Davien Beltran (Employee 316532) similarly appears under both Agency 230 and Agency 290: a retention bonus (REN) of $1,500 under Agency 230 on 03/15/2025, and a recruitment bonus (REC) of $1,500 under Agency 290 on 06/07/2025 — both within the same fiscal year.
contradictions.reference: Bonus Report: '230 316532 Davien Beltran 1 1,500.00 USD REN RETENTION-MORE THAN 6 MO 03/15/2025' and '290 316532 Davien Beltran 1 1,500.00 USD REC RECRUITMENT-MORE THAN 6 MO 06/07/2025'

contradictions.contradiction_text: The FY2025 Aeronautics revenue in the Agency Performance Report table shows State Aeronautics Fund State revenue of $5,631,561, but the Agency Revenues form (B11) shows State Aeronautics Fund - Dedicated/State (22102) FY25 actuals of $5,328,400 and the Analysis of Fund Balances (22102) shows FY25 revenues of $5,328,400. The performance report figure ($5,631,561) includes Fund 22104 interagency revenues of $303,100, reconciling the difference approximately.
contradictions.reference: Performance report p.251: 'Aeronautics Fund State FY2025 $5,631,561'; B11 Revenue p.11: '22102 State Aeronautics Fund Dedicated/State Total FY25 Actuals 5,328,400'; Fund 22104 FY25 actuals: $303,100

contradictions.contradiction_text: The CGI Advantage contract maintenance fee schedule in Amendment 24 shows Period 21 (FY2026, commencing July 1, 2025) total of $1,857,800, but the Contract Inflation form (B4 Part C) shows FY2026 Estimated Expenditures of $2,008,700 for CGI Advantage — a discrepancy of $151,300. Period 22 (FY2027) in the contract is $2,008,733, matching the FY2026 estimated expenditure figure rather than the FY2026 contract period amount.

leads.description: The Agency Summary & Certification is signed 'Larry Stokes' while all other document sections identify the Director as 'Scott Stokes' (full name L. Scott Stokes per performance report). Determine whether 'Larry' and 'Scott' are the same person (L. = Lawrence/Larry), a clerical error, or evidence of an unauthorized signature.
where_to_look: Idaho Secretary of State executive appointment records (sos.idaho.gov)
Idaho Division of Human Resources personnel directory for Agency 290
Idaho Legislature confirmation records for ITD Director appointment
Idaho Transportation Board meeting minutes (publicly posted on itd.idaho.gov)
leads.notes: The performance report on p.250 lists 'L. Scott Stokes, Director' suggesting 'L.' may be a first initial, and 'Larry' could be a nickname or error. Confirm identity.

leads.title: Jacob Stokes Employment at ITD — Potential Nepotism
leads.description: An employee named Jacob Stokes received a $1,500 recruitment bonus at ITD (Agency 290) in June 2025. The ITD Director is L. Scott Stokes. Verify whether Jacob Stokes is related to the Director and whether hiring/bonus processes complied with Idaho nepotism statutes (IC §67-5309A).
where_to_look: Idaho Division of Human Resources personnel records for Agency 290
Idaho Ethics in Government Act compliance filings
ITD internal HR records for position 311526 (public records request)
Idaho Code §67-5309A (nepotism prohibition in state employment)
leads.notes: Shared surname alone is not evidence of wrongdoing; this is a verification lead. The bonus report shows Agency 290, Employee 311526, Jacob Stokes, recruitment bonus $1,500 on 06/21/2025.

leads.title: Dual-Agency Bonus Payments — Employees Receiving Retention and Recruitment Bonuses Across Two Agencies
leads.description: Employees Phillip Borresen (310409) and Davien Beltran (316532) each appear under both Agency 230 and Agency 290 in the bonus report, receiving retention bonuses at one agency and recruitment bonuses at ITD within the same period. Verify that these inter-agency transfers complied with state personnel rules and that employees were not improperly double-compensated.
where_to_look: Idaho Division of Human Resources bonus/incentive pay policy and records
Idaho State Controller's payroll records for employees 310409 and 316532
State Personnel Commission rules on recruitment and retention incentives (IDAPA 15.04.01)
ITD HR records for positions associated with these employees
leads.notes: Borresen: Agency 230 retention $1,500 on 08/17/2024; Agency 290 recruitment $1,500 on 06/07/2025. Beltran: Agency 230 retention $1,500 on 03/15/2025; Agency 290 recruitment $1,500 on 06/07/2025. Agency 230 is Idaho Department of Fish and Game based on Idaho agency code conventions (public knowledge).

leads.title: Growing Structural Negative Cash Position in State Highway Account Dedicated Fund (26002)
leads.description: Fund 26002 ending unobligated cash balance is projected to reach -$174,203,400 by end of FY2027, with the gap growing by approximately $55M per year. The fund relies on $183,935,300 in direct investments to maintain any positive net position. Investigate whether this trajectory is sustainable and whether ITD has disclosed this to appropriators.
where_to_look: Idaho Division of Financial Management (DFM) analysis of Fund 26002 solvency
Idaho Legislative Services Office budget analysis for ITD
Idaho State Controller's Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) — Fund 26002 balances
ITD FY2025 audited financial statements
Idaho Joint Finance-Appropriations Committee (JFAC) hearing records
leads.notes: The trend: FY24 ending unobligated balance -$34.5M; FY25 -$63.6M; FY26 est. -$118.7M; FY27 est. -$174.2M. Net of investments: FY27 net positive only $9.7M. This structural issue is documented in the budget submission but may not be adequately highlighted to legislators.

leads.title: GARVEE Prior-Period Adjustment — Incorrectly Recorded Construction Costs FY2020-2022
leads.description: ITD is requesting legislative authorization for prior-period accounting adjustments of up to $303,900 for GARVEE construction costs incorrectly recorded in FY2020, FY2021, and FY2022 (DU 12.97). Determine the nature and cause of the misclassification, whether it resulted in improper federal reimbursements, and whether any similar issues may exist beyond the $303,900 disclosed.
where_to_look: Idaho Legislative Services Office review of DU 12.97 authorization request
ITD internal audit records (Jolene Crumley, Internal Review)
FHWA audit or oversight records for Idaho GARVEE projects
Idaho State Controller prior-period adjustment records under IC §67-3604
ITD FY2020-2022 audited financial statements for GARVEE Capital Project Fund (37400)
leads.notes: ITD states 'does not anticipate additional accounting adjustments,' but the 3-year span of incorrect recording warrants independent verification. Federal funds were used for GARVEE debt repayment, so misclassification could affect federal compliance.

leads.title: CGI Advantage Contract Fee Schedule Discrepancy
leads.description: The CGI Advantage contract (Amendment 24, Period 21) specifies a FY2026 (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026) maintenance total of $1,857,800, but ITD's Contract Inflation form shows FY2026 estimated expenditures of $2,008,700 — a discrepancy of $150,900. Verify which figure is correct and whether ITD is overbudgeting or if there are additional services beyond the contract schedule.
where_to_look: ITD procurement records for Contract CPO01749 and Amendment 24
Idaho Division of Purchasing (DOP) contract management system
ITD Financial Services invoices from CGI for Period 21
ITD Budget Office records (Kirk Weiskircher) reconciling contract vs. budget figures
leads.notes: The $2,008,700 figure in the B4 form matches Period 22 (FY2027) in the contract, suggesting a possible one-year offset in the contract period mapping. Supplemental maintenance services at $180-200/hour could also explain the gap.

leads.title: FMCSA Grant Funding Drop to Zero in FY2027 — CDL and Technology Programs
leads.description: Two FMCSA grants (CFDA 20.232 Commercial Driver License State Programs and CFDA 20.237 High Priority Program) are projected at $0 for FY2027. The CDL grant was $556,654 in FY2025. ITD states it 'has no plans to apply for this discretionary grant during 2027.' Verify whether this represents a genuine program decision or loss of eligibility, and the impact on CDL program quality.
where_to_look: FMCSA grant management system (grants.fmcsa.dot.gov)
Idaho DMV CDL program reports to FMCSA
ITD Federal Funds Inventory detail rows for CFDA 20.232 and 20.237
Idaho JFAC budget oversight records
leads.notes: Both grants are listed as short-term (expiring 9/30/2027 for 20.232). The drop to zero in FY2027 while the grant is still technically active through September 2027 is inconsistent. The FTA Large Urban grant (20.507) is also dropping to zero as ITD works to help Idaho Falls become a direct recipient — this transfer of recipient status warrants monitoring.

leads.title: General Fund Transfer Mismatch: $275M Offset vs. $275M in Line Item Requests
leads.description: Decision Unit 12.89 (TRFF) reflects a negative revenue adjustment of -$275,000,000 ($165M to Strategic Initiatives Program Fund + $110M to Local Highway Distribution Fund), described as a 'revenue adjustment for the cash transfer from the State of Idaho General Fund.' Meanwhile DU 12.08 and 12.09 request $87,912,800 and $187,087,200 respectively totaling $275,000,000 in positive transfers. Verify that the netting is correct and that the $275M General Fund transfer is fully appropriated and matched.
where_to_look: Idaho General Fund appropriations bill for FY2027
Idaho DFM budget analysis reconciling DU 12.08, 12.09, and 12.89
Idaho State Controller's transfer records between General Fund and Funds 27002 and 25901
Idaho JFAC budget hearing transcripts on Idaho First/Leading Idaho transportation funding
leads.notes: DU 12.08 = $87,912,800 (60% to ITD SIPF $52.7M, 40% to LHDF $35.2M); DU 12.09 = $187,087,200 (60% to ITD SIPF $112.3M, 40% to LHDF $74.8M); Total = $275,000,000. DU 12.89 offsets with -$275,000,000. The net to spending authority is zero but the gross cash flow is material.

leads.title: ITD Unfunded 'Ghost' Positions Outside FTP Cap
leads.description: ITD maintains numerous unfunded, unappropriated positions outside the legislatively authorized FTP cap, used solely for recruitment pipeline purposes. At least 20+ such positions are documented in the vacant position questionnaires. While described as a legitimate practice, these positions create phantom FTP counts in budget systems. Verify that all such positions are truly outside the FTP cap and not consuming any appropriated funds.
where_to_look: Idaho Legislature FTP cap authorization in annual appropriation bills
Idaho Division of Human Resources position control records for Agency 290
Idaho State Controller payroll records to confirm zero expenditures on these PCNs
ITD internal HR policy on unfunded recruitment positions
leads.notes: Examples include positions 12104, 12112, 12113, 12789, 12806-12810, 12823, 12841, etc. ITD states these are outside the FTP cap and not funded. However, the Vacant FTP Questionnaire is a required disclosure, suggesting legislators may not be fully aware of the scale of this practice.

leads.title: District 3 Concentration of Hard-to-Fill Vacancies Impacting Project Delivery
leads.description: Multiple funded, active vacancies are concentrated in District 3 across engineering, design/construction, and operations roles. Several vacancy questionnaires note these have caused project delays, overtime, and significant staff stress in 2025. Assess whether the concentration of vacancies in District 3 represents a systemic workforce or compensation problem requiring additional intervention.
where_to_look: ITD Workforce Development reports (Mike Stowell)
Idaho Division of Human Resources compensation surveys for transportation engineering positions
ITD District 3 performance metrics and project delivery reports
Idaho Legislative audit of ITD workforce capacity (if any)
leads.notes: Positions affected in D3 include: Technical Engineer 2 (14220), Transportation Tech Engineering Principal (14103), Transportation Tech Sr. x4 (14114, 14190, 13869, 13871), Engineering Asst (14174), Avalanche Tech (14030), and multiple entry-level engineers. The FY2025 is repeatedly described as 'very difficult' in these disclosures.
